title: What does EscrowCreate do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of EscrowCreate and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, EscrowCreate locks funds for a specified recipient until the configured time or cryptographic conditions permit release. [1]

FinishAfter and CancelAfter use ledger time, and a Condition can require a matching fulfillment. Trust-line token escrow requires the issuer's AllowTrustLineLocking permission; MPT escrow has its own capability flags. Holding a token balance alone does not establish escrow eligibility. Creation locks principal but does not pay the recipient. [1]

The EscrowCreate reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using EscrowCreate, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
